d: Egis is an international player active in architecture, consulting, construction engineering and mobility services. The Group’s operations in the Middle East are built on strategic acquisitions and a deep understanding of local market conditions. Egis has long history of providing comprehensive engineering, consulting, and project management services makes it a trusted partner for regional governments, investors, and developers.

d: The Shop Floor Planner is responsible for translating the overall production plan into practical resource-level shop floor schedules. The role focuses on capacity planning, optimum resource utilisation, work allocation, material readiness, workflow control, quality checkpoints, efficiency improvement and maximum throughput while ensuring committed completion and delivery dates are achieved.
q: Minimum 3–5 years of production/shop floor planning experience, preferably within bespoke joinery, furniture, shopfitting or similar manufacturing.
Strong understanding of joinery manufacturing processes, production routing and resource capacity planning.
Good knowledge of timber, boards, laminates, veneers, hardware and related joinery components.
Ability to read and understand production drawings, BOMs and cutting lists.
Strong analytical capability for capacity calculation, workload balancing, scheduling and performance monitoring.
Proficiency in Excel and production planning/ERP systems; exposure to joinery/CNC operations is an added advantage.
Strong coordination, communication and problem-solving skills in a fast-paced shop floor environment.
r: Calculate available capacity for each production resource, including machinery, manpower and work centres.
Maintain capacity-versus-load plans by process, considering working hours, shift patterns, planned downtime, absenteeism and realistic efficiency levels.
Identify constraints and bottlenecks in advance and recommend workload balancing, overtime, additional shifts, alternate machines or outsourcing where required.
Convert the master production plan into daily and weekly shop floor schedules.
Assign jobs to individual resources/work centres based on priority, machine capability, manpower skills, available capacity and required completion dates.
Sequence jobs to minimise idle time, excessive changeovers, waiting time and unnecessary material movement.
Review actual progress against plan and reschedule where required to protect committed delivery dates.
Coordinate with Planning, Procurement, Stores, Setting Out and Production to ensure drawings, BOMs, cutting lists, materials, hardware and other inputs are ready before work is released.
Highlight shortages and technical information gaps early to prevent production stoppages.
Establish and maintain workflow charts/routing for each job through processes such as panel processing, CNC, milling, veneering, assembly, polishing and other required operations.
Monitor WIP movement between work centres and maintain balanced flow between upstream and downstream processes.
Control job priorities and avoid excessive WIP accumulation at bottleneck operations.
Coordinate with Production and QC to include defined quality checkpoints at critical manufacturing stages.
Ensure defects and rework are identified early so they do not affect downstream operations, capacity or delivery schedules.
Monitor planned versus actual production hours, resource utilisation, productivity, machine downtime, rework and output.
Analyse causes of lost capacity and recommend practical improvements to increase efficiency and maximum throughput.
Support line balancing, job sequencing and optimum utilisation of available machinery and manpower.
Track production progress against committed completion and delivery dates.
Escalate potential delays, capacity shortages, material constraints and production risks early with recommended recovery actions.
Prepare daily/weekly reports covering capacity versus load, schedule adherence, resource utilisation, WIP status, bottlenecks, throughput and delivery risks.
